`@synap-core/sdk/connect` lets one app work on many pods: each person signs in with their own pod, chooses the
spaces the app may use, and can take that access back. The app is an OAuth 2.1 public client of each pod (PKCE S256,
the pod's `iss` checked on every answer). Its client ID is the https URL of a client metadata document that the app
serves itself, so there is nothing to register on a pod. The pod's token stays on your server, sealed in an
HTTP-only cookie; the browser never sees it.

This page is the reference. To build an app step by step, follow
[Build a website on your pod](/docs/build/build-a-website). The `AGENTS.md` file shipped in the npm package has
every rule in full.

The entry is server-only: it throws when loaded in a browser, and a browser bundle resolves it to a stub that throws.
It uses Web-standard `Request`, `Response` and WebCrypto, so it runs in Next.js route handlers and `proxy.ts`, Hono,
Remix and edge runtimes. It needs Node.js 20 or later.

## Set up: `createPodAppAuth`

```ts title="lib/synap.ts"
import { createPodAppAuth } from "@synap-core/sdk/connect";

export const synap = createPodAppAuth({
  appUrl: process.env.SYNAP_APP_URL!, // https://notes.example.com
  clientName: "Notes",
  requests: [
    { permission: "entity.note.read", reason: "Show your notes" },
    { permission: "entity.note.create", reason: "Save the notes you write here" },
  ],
  secret: process.env.SYNAP_APP_SESSION_SECRET!,
});
```

| Option | What it is |
|---|---|
| `appUrl` | Your app's origin: https, a domain name (not an IP address), no path, query or fragment. `http://localhost` is accepted, but only the SDK's mock pod signs in an app served over http. |
| `clientName` | The name the consent screen shows, 1 to 100 characters. |
| `requests` | What the app asks for: 1 to 48 entries (duplicates count), each `{ permission, reason, scope? }`. See [Permissions](#permissions). |
| `secret` | Seals the cookies. At least 32 characters, server-side only. Pass several to rotate. |
| `templates` | Optional. Up to 8 template slugs the consent screen may offer to create as a space. |
| `paths` | Optional. Overrides for the routes below. Each is an absolute path on your app. |
| `store` | Optional. Where the connection is kept. Default: the sealed cookie. See [Your own store](#your-own-store). |
| `resource` | Optional. `"api/hub"` (default), `"mcp"` or `null`: the pod API the token is for. |
| `cloudUrl` | Optional. The Synap Cloud URL, to offer "Continue with Synap Cloud". See [Synap Cloud](#synap-cloud). |
| `allowInsecureLoopback` | Optional. Accept a pod, or a Synap Cloud, served on `http://localhost`, for development. |
| `onError` | Optional. Called with each refused sign-in, for your logs. Default: `console.warn`. Messages never carry a token. |
| `fetch` | Optional. Your own `fetch`. |

`createPodAppAuth` refuses at startup, with a `ConnectError` whose code is `misconfigured`, every setup the pod would
refuse at sign-in, so the mistake shows when your app starts, not when a person connects. The client metadata
document must stay under 8 KB.

## Routes

| Path (default) | Method | Handler | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/.well-known/synap-client.json` | GET | `handlers.clientMetadata` | Serves the client metadata document. Its URL is the client ID. |
| `/api/synap/connect` | POST | `handlers.connect` | Starts the sign-in for the pod named in the form. |
| `/api/synap/callback` | GET | `handlers.callback` | Takes the pod's answer, stores the connection, redirects to `next`. |
| `/api/synap/disconnect` | POST | `handlers.disconnect` | Revokes the token at the pod and clears the cookie. |
| `/api/synap/cloud` | POST, GET | `handlers.cloudConnect`, `handlers.cloudReturn` | Synap Cloud sign-in, when `cloudUrl` is set. |

Three more paths are pages of your app: `/connect` (the connect page; the pod may send people there to start a
sign-in), `/connect/result` (where a failed callback lands with `?error=<code>`) and `/` (where a sign-in lands when
it named no `next`). Each route file re-exports one handler, for example `export const POST = synap.handlers.connect;`.

`connect` and `disconnect` change state, so they accept a `POST` from your own pages only (the `Origin` header, or
`Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`). The connect form sends:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pod` | The pod's address, as the person typed it. `https://` is added when it is missing. |
| `next` | Optional. A path on your app to land on after sign-in. |
| `space` | Optional. A space to suggest on the consent screen. A pod may ignore it: never rely on a space being preselected. |
| `prompt` | Optional. `consent` shows the consent screen again even when this browser is already connected (to widen or narrow access); `login` asks the person to sign in to the pod again. |

Before it sends the browser anywhere, the SDK reads the pod's OAuth metadata and checks that it is a Synap pod that
supports app sign-in. It never follows a redirect from the pod: a pod that moved answers `pod_moved`, and the person
connects again with the new address. The connect route fetches an address a visitor typed, so rate-limit it per
visitor.

## Permissions

Each request names one permission in the pod's grammar, `<subject>[.<qualifier>].<action>`, lowercase, as in
[API key grants](/docs/build/api-keys), and the sentence the consent screen shows (`reason`, 1 to 200 characters).
The person ticks what the app gets; asking is not getting.

| Rule | Example |
|---|---|
| No wildcard: name what you ask for. | `entity.note.read`, not `entity.*` |
| A subject and at least one more segment. | `entity.note` (every action on notes) is accepted; `document` alone is not. |
| A qualifier only on `entity` (a kind), `capability` (an intent) and `event` (a family). | `entity.post.create`, `capability.publish_post.run`, `event.dev.read` |
| On an intent, `run` is the only action. | `capability.send_message.run` |
| `scope: "pod"` only on a read of one kind. Everything else is given per space. | `{ permission: "entity.decision.read", reason, scope: "pod" }` |

A pod-wide read comes back as a grant row with no space: `listEntities({ profileSlug })` with no `workspaceId` then
lists that kind across the pod. Writes always name a space the person granted.

## The connection

After sign-in the connection holds the pod's URL, the person (`user`), the grant by space and the tokens.

| | |
|---|---|
| Access token | Lives 1 hour. |
| Refresh token | Rotates on each use and lives 30 days from issue. A spent refresh token presented again within a short grace (30 seconds by default) gets the same new pair; after it, the pod revokes the whole connection. |
| Session cookie | `__Host-synap_session` on https, sealed with AES-GCM. |
| Marker cookie | `__Host-synap_seen`, 400 days: the pod's URL only, so a lapsed connection reads as "expired", not "never connected". A disconnect clears it. |

Read the connection where you have the request, or its `Cookie` header:

```ts
const connection = await synap.readConnection((await headers()).get("cookie"));
if (!connection) redirect("/connect");
```

`synap.readLapsed(cookieHeader)` answers `{ podUrl }` when this browser was connected to a pod and the connection
lapsed, so you can say "expired, connect again" with the address pre-filled.

### Renewal

A server component cannot set cookies, so renew in `proxy.ts` (or a route handler) before the page renders:
`synap.refreshIfNeeded(request)` rotates the token only in its last 5 minutes, and only once at a time per connection
in the process. Send `outcome.setCookies` on the response and forward `outcome.cookieHeader` as the request's
`Cookie`. [Build a website on your pod](/docs/build/build-a-website) has the full `proxy.ts`, with the matcher that
skips static files, the sign-in routes and router prefetches.

| `status` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `none` | No connection in this request (`lapsed` set when there was one). |
| `skipped` | A prefetch or a static asset: nothing renewed. |
| `fresh` | Valid beyond the renewal window, or no refresh token. |
| `refreshed` | Rotated: send `setCookies`, forward `cookieHeader`. |
| `kept` | The refresh failed but the access token still works. Not asked again for a minute. |
| `expired` | The access token is spent and cannot be renewed: connect again. |
| `revoked` | The pod refused the refresh token (access removed): connect again. |
| `unavailable` | The pod could not be reached and the access token is spent: try later. |

In a route handler or a server action, `synap.client(connection, { request, persist })` renews once after a `401`
and retries the request once; `persist` receives the `Set-Cookie` values to send. Without `persist` (a server
component), a `401` answers `unauthorized` with `refreshable: true`: send the visitor through the proxy with
`refreshIfNeeded(request, { force: true })`.

## The client: `synap.client(connection)`

```ts
const pod = synap.client(connection);

const notes = await pod.listEntities({ workspaceId, profileSlug: "note", limit: 50 });
if (!notes.ok) console.warn(notes.error.code);

const res = await pod.post("/entities", { profileSlug: "note", workspaceId, title: "Hello" });
if (res.ok && res.status === "proposed") showPending(res.reviewUrl);
```

Calls never throw: a read answers `{ ok: true, data }` or `{ ok: false, error }`. A write answers one of:

| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `{ ok: true, status: "applied", data }` | The pod applied the write. |
| `{ ok: true, status: "proposed", proposalId, reviewUrl, data }` | The write waits for the person's review. This is a success: show `reviewUrl`, never retry. |
| `{ ok: false, error }` | Refused or failed; see [Error codes](#error-codes). |

`get`, `post`, `patch`, `put` and `delete` take a Hub REST path (`/entities`, not `/api/hub/entities`); see the
[Hub REST API](/docs/reference/hub-api). Encode each path segment with `encodeURIComponent`: a path that could leave
the Hub answers `invalid` without a request. Typed reads include `listEntities`, `getEntity`, `getEntityConnections`,
`getDocument`, `getFileUrl` and `listPendingProposals` (needs `proposal.read`).

| Member | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| `actsAs` | `"agent"` for every app except Synap's official ones (`"person"`). An agent's writes are proposals, and an agent never approves. |
| `spaces()` | The granted spaces: `{ workspaceId, workspaceName, permissions }`, plus `templateSlug` when the pod names the template the space came from. |
| `podWide()` | The reads approved pod-wide. |
| `can(permission, workspaceId?)` | Whether the grant covers a permission, read with the pod's grammar (`entity.read` covers `entity.note.read`). |
| `reach(permission)` | Where the connection holds it: `{ kind: "pod" }`, `{ kind: "spaces", ids }` or `null`. |
| `rateLimit()` | The budget the pod's last answer named: `{ limit, remaining, resetSec, at }`, or `null`. |
| `actions` | `actions.list` and `actions.request`: ask the person's own tools to do something (needs `capability.<intent>.run`). An intent that reaches outside the pod, such as posting or sending a message, always comes back `proposed`. |

Client options: `timeoutMs` (default 10 000; a slower request answers `pod_unreachable`), `maxResponseBytes`
(default 8 MiB; a bigger answer is `server`) and `retryRateLimitedWithinSec` (default 0: a `GET` answered `429` with a
wait at most this long is asked once more after the wait; writes are never retried).

### Rate limits

A pod budgets the calls each connection makes in a 15-minute window, with separate budgets for reads and writes (by
default 3,000 reads and 500 writes; the pod's owner can change them). Over the budget, every call answers
`rate_limited` with `retryAfterSec` until the window ends. Read a list once per page and keep it for that request,
rather than asking again.

## Error codes

A call's `error` is `{ code, status, retryAfterSec?, detail?, podCode?, reason? }`. Branch on `code`; `detail` and
`podCode` are for your logs. `status` is `null` when nothing was answered, and `reason` is set when the SDK refused
without sending anything (`not_granted`, `agent_cannot_approve`, `invalid_input`). `POD_ERROR_CODES` lists every code.

| `code` | What to do |
|---|---|
| `expired` | The connection's time is up: connect again. |
| `unauthorized` | The pod refused the token; with `refreshable`, renew once (see [Renewal](#renewal)). |
| `forbidden` | The person did not grant this, or an agent tried to approve. |
| `door_unsupported` | The pod is too old for this call. |
| `not_found` | It does not exist, or the app cannot read it. |
| `invalid` | The request is malformed. |
| `conflict` | Someone changed it first: read again. |
| `rate_limited` | Wait `retryAfterSec`. |
| `pod_unreachable` | No answer, or a timeout: try later. |
| `pod_moved` | The pod answered a redirect: connect again with its new address. |
| `step_up_required` | The person must confirm at their pod first. |
| `email_unverified` | Synap Cloud needs a verified email. |
| `origin_insecure` | Synap Cloud needs the app on https. |
| `server` | The pod failed, or answered something the SDK cannot read. |

A sign-in that fails redirects with `?error=<code>`: to your connect page when it could not start, to your result
page when it failed on the way back. `parseConnectErrorCode(value)` reads it back (`null` for anything else).

| Sign-in `error` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `invalid_pod_address` | The address is not a usable URL. |
| `not_a_pod` | Something answered, but it is not a Synap pod. |
| `pod_unreachable` | The pod did not answer. |
| `pod_unsupported` | A Synap pod too old for app sign-in. |
| `cp_unavailable` | Synap Cloud is not configured for this app. |
| `denied` | The person said no on the consent screen. |
| `expired_transaction` | No sign-in in progress, or it is older than 10 minutes. |
| `mismatch` | The answer does not belong to the sign-in this browser started. |
| `misconfigured` | The app's own setup is wrong. |
| `rate_limited` | The pod asked to slow down. |
| `expired`, `revoked` | The connection lapsed, or the pod refused its refresh token. |
| `pod_moved` | The pod moved: connect again with its new address. |
| `server_error` | The pod answered something the SDK cannot use. |

## Synap Cloud

With `cloudUrl` set, `synap.cloudConnectAvailable` is `true` and the app can offer "Continue with Synap Cloud": a
`POST` to `handlers.cloudConnect` sends the browser to the Synap Cloud pod chooser, which returns to your connect page.
There, `acceptLaunch(url, origin).cloudState` is set: forward the request's query to `handlers.cloudReturn`, which
checks the return against this browser's cookie before the chosen pod is used, then signs in as with a typed address.

```tsx title="app/connect/page.tsx"
const launch = acceptLaunch(url, origin);
if (launch.cloudState) redirect(`${synap.paths.cloud}${new URL(url).search}`);
```

## Your own store

By default the connection lives in the sealed cookie. To keep it in a database or a key-value store, implement
`ConnectionStore` and pass it as `store`:

```ts
interface ConnectionStore {
  read(request: Request): Promise<PodConnection | null>;
  write(connection: PodConnection, request: Request): Promise<string[]>; // Set-Cookie values
  clear(request: Request): Promise<string[]>;
}
```

A shared server-side store also protects a connection served by several server instances: the pod revokes a
connection when a spent refresh token is presented again, and only one store all instances read can rule that out.

## Test without a pod

`@synap-core/sdk/testing` has `createMockAuthServer()`, a mock pod with the metadata, the consent step, the token,
refresh and revoke endpoints and the Hub doors an app uses, and `createMockCloud()` for the Synap Cloud chooser.
Pass the mock's `fetch` to `createPodAppAuth`; the mock answers in memory, so your app can run on
`http://localhost`. A real pod, even a local one, accepts only an app served over https: use a tunnel in development.

```ts
import { createMockAuthServer } from "@synap-core/sdk/testing";

const pod = createMockAuthServer({ actsAs: "agent" });
const synap = createPodAppAuth({ ...config, fetch: pod.fetch });
```
